The paintings

Source: vignettes/articles/paintings.Rmd
paintings.Rmd

Each palette is drawn from one or more works by Candido Portinari (1903–1962). Eight are in the collection of the Museu de Arte de São Paulo (MASP); Guerra and Paz are the two panels he painted for the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Click an image or title to open the work’s page.

The palettes are an interpretation of each work’s dominant tones, not a measurement of it. The exception is terra_roxa, whose colors were sampled from the MASP images: the purples of the worker’s shirt and Queiroz Lima’s suit, and the pale greens of the coffee rows and hills. Images are shown from the MASP collection site and remain under copyright.

cafe

Qualitative · 6 colors · colorblind-friendly

Warm coffee-plantation tones: brick, ochre and cream, with a blue counterpoint.

retirantes

Diverging · 8 colors · colorblind-friendly

Cool slate to warm earth through cream: the dusty tones of the Migrant series and portraits.

inah

Diverging · 5 colors · first 4 colorblind-safe

Dusk blue and sage to blush and ochre, through cream.

sofia

Diverging · 5 colors · first 3 colorblind-safe

Deep green and teal to gold and rose, through cream.

terra_roxa

Diverging · 9 colors · colorblind-friendly

Plum and mauve to pale coffee greens through sage off-white.

guerra

Diverging · 9 colors · colorblind-friendly

A symphony in blue, from deep violet-indigo to pale citrine, against an orange, rose and red counterpoint.

paz

Qualitative · 8 colors · first 4 colorblind-safe

Golden yellows of a ‘golden age’, with ochre, orange, rose, olive and sky blue.

Derived sequential palettes

guerra_azul and paz_ouro are taken from the panels above: the blue scale of Guerra and the earth-to-gold run of Paz, ordered from dark to light.
